title: India Passes US as ChatGPT's Largest Market as Users Double
excerpt: OpenAI India chief Prabhjeet Singh says India's weekly active users have doubled since January and passed the US; CEO Sam Altman said the same on a November 3 podcast.
body:
• India has become ChatGPT's largest market by weekly active users, overtaking the United States, according to OpenAI India managing director Prabhjeet Singh in an interview with The Economic Times reported by Indian Startup News.
  • Singh said India's user base has doubled since January 2026; OpenAI had put India above 100 million weekly users in February, when it was still the second-largest market.
  • OpenAI CEO Sam Altman corroborated the ranking on Raj Shamani's Figuring Out podcast released November 3, saying: "India is our biggest market in the world by ChatGPT users and growing very quickly."
  • What it means for users in India: OpenAI is expanding ads on Free and Go plans, says announcements on UPI and payments are expected in the coming weeks, and is prioritising Hindi and vernacular voice support and entry-level Android phones.

Two OpenAI leaders, the same ranking

India is now ChatGPT's largest market in the world by weekly active users, overtaking the United States, according to OpenAI India managing director Prabhjeet Singh. Singh — OpenAI's first managing director for India, appointed in June — made the remarks in an interview with The Economic Times, his first since taking the role, as reported by Indian Startup News.

https://x.com/YourStoryCo/status/2117900559936315891

The ranking does not rest on that interview alone. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the same thing independently on Raj Shamani's Figuring Out podcast, released on November 3, 2026: "India is our biggest market in the world by ChatGPT users and growing very quickly," according to BestMediaInfo's summary of the podcast.

"In less than a year, it's doubling. It just gives you a sense of (how) people are beginning to find relevance and deep use cases."

— Prabhjeet Singh, OpenAI India managing director

What "largest" actually measures

The measure is weekly active users: anyone who opens ChatGPT at least once in a week, across free and paid tiers. Indian Startup News notes it is the only usage number OpenAI discloses, and OpenAI has not published a fresh absolute count alongside the new ranking. The last disclosed figure was in February, when Altman said India had passed 100 million weekly users and was the second-largest market, with the largest number of student users anywhere. Singh said the base has since doubled compared with January 2026. Because the 100 million figure dates from February and the doubling is measured from January, a precise current total cannot be calculated from the two disclosures — and this article does not invent one.

How second place became first

The climb was built on price and presence, according to Indian Startup News. OpenAI announced plans in August 2025 to open its first India office in Delhi NCR and began hiring locally. The same month it launched ChatGPT Go, a plan priced at under $5 a month, then made Go free for a year to Indian users who signed up from November 4, 2025. At the India AI Impact Summit in February, OpenAI launched its OpenAI for India programme and said it would add offices in Mumbai and Bengaluru. Altman said then that 18- to 24-year-olds account for nearly half of ChatGPT usage in the country.

Singh's stated priority is the users still outside that base. "Most of India actually doesn't use English as a primary. So real big focus is on Hindi and vernacular," he said. The work, as reported, runs three ways: more Indian-language voice support, product work for entry-level Android phones with little spare memory, and Android-first development.

The business behind the users

Adoption is not the same as revenue. India's mobile app market hit a record $345 million in consumer spending in the June quarter, up 35 percent year-on-year, according to Sensor Tower figures cited by Indian Startup News, while US app revenue fell 3 percent. ChatGPT was the most downloaded app in India, with cumulative downloads past 358 million, the report said.

OpenAI is now expanding advertising in India on the Free and Go plans, and Singh said announcements on UPI and payments are expected in the coming weeks. OpenAI has also signed Indian data-centre capacity through TCS's HyperVault, starting at 100 megawatts and potentially scaling to 1 gigawatt, according to the same report.

What to watch next

For diaspora readers who split their digital lives between India and the US, the ranking matters for product decisions, not bragging rights: language support, pricing tiers, payments via UPI and local data residency are all being set first for the market with the most users. The concrete markers to watch are the promised UPI announcement in the coming weeks, how far Hindi and vernacular voice support extends beyond the current base, and whether OpenAI ever discloses an absolute weekly-user figure for India to replace February's 100 million.
